subject: MSA/Order Form: confidentiality redlines + reference/asset permissions (Acme)
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Rebecca Stone <rebecca.stone@acmeinc.com>
Cc: legal@acmeinc.com
Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2029 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/Order Form: confidentiality redlines + reference/asset permissions (Acme)

Hi team,

Attaching the customer-facing order form (v3 redline) and the draft case study Acme shared. Legal raised a few points during the procurement review and I want to capture an operational path forward before we escalate pricing/credits. High level:

- Confidentiality: Acme's counsel is pushing a broader "confidential information" carveout for performance metrics and usage numbers. They want those treated as confidential unless explicitly approved for public use.
- Publicity / reference rights: Acme asks for a near-unrestricted right to reference Redwood in press and collateral ("reference rights"), plus a license to use logos. Legal wants a more constrained permission set and an approval step for quotes/quotes' attribution.
- Logo use & assets: Acme would like logo files in vector format and permission for use in slide decks and press kits. They asked for perpetual, royalty-free usage in the order form; legal flagged that as too broad.
- Evidence & case study approval: We typically require a 2-step approval: (1) quote approval (15 business days), (2) final case study signoff. Acme's draft shortens timelines.

Action items I propose:
1) Agree a tailored confidentiality definition that explicitly exempts aggregated, de-identified metrics for Redwood internal benchmarking and marketing (so we can talk about "pilot increased throughput by X%"), while protecting raw customer data and PII.
2) Provide Acme a limited, non-exclusive logo grant for marketing materials and press with mandatory prior-approval for any press release (we ask for 10 business days' notice).
3) Insert a two-signoff process for any customer quotes/case studies with a maximum review window of 10 business days; if no response, approvals are deemed granted (only for non-sensitive excerpts).
4) Offer to host an evidence/metrics snapshot in a controlled artifact (redwood-reference-guidelines-2029.pdf) rather than embedding raw data in the case study.

Please see the attached redline PDFs (ACME_Order_Form_v3_redline.pdf) and the draft case study (acme_case_study_draft.docx). Rebecca — can you confirm whether Acme's legal team is open to these guardrails?

Thanks,

--
Olga Petrov

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: confidentiality redlines + reference/asset permissions (Acme)

Thanks, Olga — high level, I agree with the proposed path. A couple of operational tweaks from the account / sales side:

- We should be explicit that anonymized, aggregated metrics (e.g., "increased throughput by 32% during a 30-day pilot") may be published without PII or identifiable telemetry. That keeps marketing momentum.
- For logo files, let's provide the EPS/PNG set and a short brand usage checklist (we have "redwood-reference-guidelines-2029.pdf" attached).
- On the deemed-approval: I prefer 10 business days with one automated reminder at day 7. If no reply, escalate to the AM and legal.

If legal will not accept "deemed approval", can we offer a one-time expedited review (48 hours) in exchange for a small implementation credit? Might be a useful concession to close the order form quickly.

Marcus
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: confidentiality redlines + reference/asset permissions (Acme)

Hi all,

I've looked through ACME's redlines (attached) and the core legal asks are:

1) Broad confidentiality of "performance data" — Acme wants the contract to classify any usage or performance metrics as Confidential by default. That's a departure from our standard. Proposed compromise language: "Performance metrics shall be treated as Confidential Information only where they are tied to raw logs or PII. Aggregated or anonymized metrics shall not be considered Confidential and may be used by Redwood for benchmarking and marketing provided individual customer identifiers are removed."

2) Publicity license — Acme's draft grants a perpetual, irrevocable license to use our name and logo in marketing. We need: a limited license to Acme for customer-provided logos and a mandatory approval right for press releases and case studies. Suggested clause: "Customer may reference Provider's name and trademark in customary customer reference contexts with Provider's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. Press releases require a minimum of 10 business days' prior written notice and approval of the release text."

3) Escrow/evidence: If they insist on showing specific numbers, require an anonymized appendix hosted on a gated drive (we can provide a snapshot and a redaction log).

4) Remedy/credit for expedited review: Negotiable — pricing team to advise.

I'll draft clean language and propose insertion points in the MSA/order form. Rebecca — if Acme legal can accept the "aggregated metrics not confidential" phrase and the 10 business day notice, we can likely close without a credit. If they insist on perpetual publicity rights, we'll need to charge for a broader marketing rights license.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: confidentiality redlines + reference/asset permissions (Acme)

Olga / Kimberly / Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and for calling out the tradeoffs. I'm looping in Acme's legal counsel (copied) to get final confirmation on the confidentiality language, but a few immediate notes from the business side:

- Acme's product marketing team needs the logo files and short usage guidance to populate our launch collateral. Could you send the EPS and a one-pager on allowed treatments?
- On metrics: Acme can accept the proposed "aggregated metrics" carveout for marketing, provided any metrics used in press include a short method note ("results based on internal pilot run; may not be representative"). That's an easy addition for us.
- On timing: 10 business days for press release approval is reasonable. Legal will confirm whether deemed approval is acceptable — if not, they'll request a standard approval loop without deemed consent.

I'll flag the attachments to legal and we should have a signed order form back within 5 business days once Kimberly's clean language lands in the doc.

Best,
Rebecca Stone
